source_span: The historical pattern is overwhelmingly that markets tend to underprice the extent of hiking cycles at the beginning... markets tend to underestimate, rather than overestimate the extent of hiking cycles.
source_chain: Fed/ECB/BoJ are hiking again, and markets are pricing more to come, therefore history (1994: 140bps priced vs 300bps delivered; 2022: 200bps priced vs 400bps delivered, among other cycles) shows investors systematically underprice hiking cycles at the start, therefore investors should expect this cycle to run hotter/longer than current pricing implies, especially given fresh commodity-driven inflation not yet in the data and looser financial conditions than in 2022 (no explicit single invalidation given; it's a probabilistic risk case, not a level-based call).
pulse_chain: Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% (unanimous, first in three years) and futures price 75bps more by June (Deutsche Bank/Reid), therefore the market has guessed short before -- 1994 (140bps priced vs 300bps delivered) and 2022 (200bps priced vs 400bps delivered), both correctly cited to Deutsche Bank -- and the oil-rate correlation at a 35-year high (Cboe, +65%) means an oil shock now doubles as a rate shock, therefore Goldman's counter-case (one more 25bp hike on Oct 27-28 then flat, based on core PCE at a 2.5% annualized 3-month pace) needs cooling data that August didn't deliver (core PCE +0.27% m/m, still above 3% y/y, correctly attributed to Goldman's own Sept 22 note), and the Fed's reaction function has hawkishly overcorrected (four participants see a hike at every remaining meeting, per Siegel), therefore whether the 10yr closes above 5% before the October meeting settles it, with BTIG's ~4.92% level as the line that would flip the trend the other way.
why: Every load-bearing figure and attribution in the chain -- Deutsche Bank's 1994/2022 underestimation stats and 75bps-by-June figure, Goldman's Oct 27-28/2.5%-PCE/0.27%-print short-cycle call, Cboe's 65% oil-yield correlation, Siegel's four-hawks detail, and BTIG's 4.92% level -- traces exactly to its named source with the same direction and no swapped invalidation, so the note's core mechanism (markets systematically underprice hiking cycles, hence more tightening than priced) survives intact even though the pulse compresses and adds a genuine bank-vs-bank debate DB's note didn't itself construct.
